record.finding: Calling the caveats appropriate scope ignores that output-size and expected-hash assumptions are absent from the requested unconditional all-pairs bound. The record may contain true conditional claims, but it does not establish the promised answer under the unchanged stem. Coherent resolution erases the decisive obstacle.

choice_reason_findings.0: A comparison-sort worst-case lower bound on unrestricted keys would justify the mismatch; sorting in general need not require n log n. The frozen solution gives no comparison-sort derivation. Identifying a qualified hash-map method does not itself rule out every other method.
choice_reason_findings.1: Enumerating all index pairs is quadratic, a valid decisive mismatch. The added claim that identifying a hash-map answer itself contradicts this alternative is invalid exclusion reasoning and repeats an unqualified hash-map premise. The distractor label need not be called factually wrong to reject this rationale as fully grounded.
choice_reason_findings.2: n searches by binary search have a standard n log n worst-case search bound after sorting, but that is new algorithm analysis rather than entailment from this frozen record. An all-index-pairs result can add quadratic output work. The stated hash-map selection cannot by itself refute alternatives.
choice_reason_findings.3: The explanation reduces the full record to hash lookups and repeats O(n) total time. It omits the explicit O(n + output pairs), quadratic-output counterexample and expected-versus-worst-case caveats. A method-name match is not entailment of the requested guarantee.
